keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Habesh row; its Ottoman shapes cover the Hejaz but not the African coast, e.g. the 1856 shape has bbox 15.8-48.6 E, 12.7-45.4 N). Infobox 503,000 km2 for 1856; the Hejaz region plus the Red Sea Sudan coast and a 60 km disc at Massawa is about 547,000 km2 on the grid (ratio 1.09). Not drawn: the highland and Zeila reach ("extended from Suakin and their hinterlands to Zeila"). Review repair 2026-10-19: ends in 1864. The 1813-1827 and 1846-1849 administration of Muhammad Ali is not a change of this shape: the page has Muhammad Ali "received the administration of Habesh in 1813" and the province "reverted to Ottoman rule in 1827", with "his son Ahmad Tushun Pasha ... appointed wali by a firman", so it is drawn as a change of administrator (rename events in the ledger), not as loss and gain. The overlap with Cliopatria's Muhammad Ali dynasty shapes is for me-10 and the renderer to resolve. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the Hejaz part is cut back from the whole Hejaz region (1,407 cells) to the Jeddah coast (a 50 km disc round Jeddah). Habesh Eyalet page: the eyalet 'included the coast of Hejaz', 'with Jeddah for its chief town'; Burckhardt in 1829 called the pashalik of Jeddah 'reduced to perfect insignificance' by the power of the Sharif of Mecca. Sharifate of Mecca page: 'Ottoman authority was only indirect, as the arrangement left real power with the Emir'; 'A dual system of government existed over Mecca for much of this period'. Mecca, Medina and the interior stay with sharifate-of-mecca; the width of the coastal strip is not on any page (my reading).

ledger.note: 1813: Muhammad Ali receives the administration of Habesh. "he received the administration of Habesh in 1813"; "His son Ahmad Tushun Pasha was appointed wali by a firman, thus also gaining control over the ports of Sawakin and Massawa." Caption only (review repair 2026-10-19): the page makes it a change of administrator of the Ottoman eyalet, "only temporary", so the land and the colour stay with this dossier; the first draft recorded a loss to muhammad-ali-dynasty.
1827: the administration returns to the Ottomans. "it reverted to Ottoman rule in 1827". Caption only; replaces the first draft's gain from muhammad-ali-dynasty.

1846: Massawa and Suakin pass to Muhammad Ali again. "Massawa and Sawakin were given to him again in 1846, until his death in 1849." Caption only, as in 1813: the ports stay in this dossier's shape under his administration.
1849: Massawa and Suakin return to the Ottoman governors at Muhammad Ali's death ("until his death in 1849"). Caption only.

1865: the African coast leaves the eyalet. Turkiyah page: "In 1865 the Ottoman Empire ceded the Red Sea coast and its ports to Egypt"; "The Red Sea ports of Suakin and Massawa came under their control." Habesh Eyalet page: "In 1866, however, Habesh was taken away from Jeddah and formally incorporated into the Egyptian vice-kingdom as a separate entity" and "starting from 1869" it was "replaced by a series of subsequent Egyptian governorates". The year follows the Turkiyah page and the turco-egyptian-sudan dossier (/ledger/10, a 1865 gain from the Ottoman Empire), so that the coast is not drawn twice; 1866 is the formal incorporation. The counterpart is the Sudan colony, which holds the coast in its keyframes, not the khedivate of the first draft.

ledger.note: 1872: Habesh Eyalet is disestablished (infobox "Disestablished: 1872"); the walilik of Jeddah, abolished for a year, "was brought back the following year", and the Hejaz continues as an Ottoman province ("transformed into the Hejaz Vilayet, with a governor in Mecca", no year on the page). The African coast has been Egyptian since 1865. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the region is the Jeddah coast, as in the 1865 keyframe (Mecca, Medina and the interior were the Sharif's: Sharifate of Mecca page, 'Ottoman authority was only indirect').

notes:
New dossier of type colony: the Ottoman province of Habesh (1557-1872), which Cliopatria lacks (its Ottoman shapes cover the Hejaz, not the African coast). One page opened (Habesh Eyalet; budget 1-2). Disagreements: the Turkiyah page (turco-egyptian-sudan dossier) has the Ottoman Empire cede the coast to Egypt in 1865, this page dates the Egyptian incorporation to 1866; 1872 (infobox) against the 1869 replacement by Egyptian governorates. Not on the page: the naib of Massawa and Arkiko, Hergigo, the Bahr Negash relation, and the extent 'extended from Suakin and their hinterlands to Zeila'. The Hejaz half (Jeddah, Medina, Mecca) is drawn here only because the infobox area (503,000 km2) includes it; the me-10 Ottoman dossier should decide whether to keep the Hejaz in the Ottoman shape or in this colony. Gazetteer: Suakin not found (coordinate approximate).
Review repair (2026-10-19): (1) 1866-1872 now the Hejaz only; the African coast leaves in 1865 (counterpart turco-egyptian-sudan, source the Turkiyah page) so it is not drawn by both dossiers; the Habesh Eyalet page itself dates the formal incorporation into the Egyptian vice-kingdom to 1866 and the replacement by governorates to 1869. The successor list keeps only the Hejaz (ottoman-empire). Jeddah is the capital from 1865 (a bridge). (2) Muhammad Ali's administration (1813-1827; Massawa and Suakin 1846-1849) is recorded as caption-only rename events, not loss/gain: the page makes it a change of administrator by firman, 'only temporary', and the eyalet's shape did not change. Disagreement with the reviewer's first option (split the keyframe): a split would leave a keyframe with no land for 1813-1826. (3) The territory quotes now follow the page verbatim ('It extended on the areas of coastal Hejaz and Northeast Africa of Eritrea that border the Red Sea basin'; 'the eyalet extended from Suakin and their hinterlands to Zeila'); the first draft's quotation marks held paraphrases. Not on the page: any governor named for 1827-1846 or 1849-1866, any year for the Hejaz Vilayet, the naib of Massawa. Gazetteer: Jeddah is in the gazetteer (39.22 E, 21.52 N used). fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the Hejaz part of the 1557 and 1865 keyframes, ledger/0, ledger/6 and successors[0].land is the Jeddah coast (50 km round Jeddah), not the whole Hejaz region: the interior belonged to the Sharif of Mecca (Sharifate of Mecca page).
